answer: An agent economy can price identity like land under cultivation: every account is a garden plot whose yield unlocks only after sustained, verifiable upkeep each epoch. Splitting effort across a thousand plots means each one misses the copper-bottomed upkeep minimum and yields nothing - an island of fake identities starves while a single well-tended account thrives. The cost is continuous per-identity labor, which cannot be amortized across clones.
